name: Crambin

highlight_material.residue_selection: CYS 3, CYS 4, CYS 16, CYS 26, CYS 32, CYS 40

artistic_notes: Crambin's three disulfide bonds define its fold; emphasize them as golden spheres against the secondary structure ribbon. The compact 46-residue frame rewards tight framing with high-contrast ss coloring to reveal its helix-sheet topology.

name: B-DNA Dodecamer
artistic_notes: The canonical B-form double helix is best presented as ball-and-stick with CPK coloring so the phosphate backbone (orange P) and base pairs (purine/pyrimidine planes) read distinctly. A faint SES surface overlay communicates the major/minor groove geometry without obscuring atomic detail.

name: Hemoglobin

highlight_material.residue_selection: HEM A, HEM B, HEM C, HEM D

artistic_notes: Color each of the four subunits (alpha1, alpha2, beta1, beta2) a distinct hue so the tetrameric assembly reads at a glance, then accent the four heme porphyrin rings as stick-and-atom detail in gold. The slight emission on the heme irons captures the iron's biologically active character.

name: ATP Synthase

highlight_material.residue_selection: ATP, ADP, Pi binding sites on beta subunits

artistic_notes: ATP synthase's rotary mechanism is the visual story; use per-chain SES surface to delineate the F1 head, central stalk, and Fo membrane ring as distinct assemblies. Semi-transparent surface over internal cartoon reveals the rotating gamma subunit axis and catalytic beta-subunit conformational asymmetry.

name: SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease (Mpro)
artistic_notes: Render the homodimer with a cool-to-warm spectrum ribbon so domain I, II, and III map from blue to red, immediately communicating the three-domain architecture. The catalytic dyad (His41/Cys145) and the bound N3 inhibitor should be rendered as atomic sticks in the active site cleft to emphasize drug-binding context.

name: Green Fluorescent Protein (GFP)
artistic_notes: GFP's eleven-strand beta-barrel is its signature; render it with ss coloring so the barrel staves read as blue sheets enclosing the chromophore. A high emission value (0.35) on the Ser65-Tyr66-Gly67 chromophore triad mimics its actual fluorescence and is the key visual hook for any publication figure.

name: Insulin Hexamer
artistic_notes: The insulin hexamer arranges as three dimers around two axial zinc ions; assign each dimer pair a distinct hue and render zinc atoms as large metallic spheres (metallic 0.15, emission 0.10) to emphasize the coordination center that drives hexamer stability. SAS overlay communicates the overall globular storage form.

name: p53 Tumor Suppressor — DNA Complex
artistic_notes: Render the p53 tetramer in warm red/orange tones and the DNA duplex as dark blue sticks to create an immediate protein-DNA contrast that conveys transcriptional regulation. The hotspot contact residues Arg248 and Arg273 deserve large sphere rendering at the protein-DNA interface to highlight the oncogenic mutation context.

name: Glutamine Synthetase

highlight_material.residue_selection: AMP-PNP, Mn2+ ions, active site loops

artistic_notes: Glutamine synthetase's twelve identical subunits form two face-to-face hexameric rings; assign each subunit a stepped hue within a cool palette and render from slightly above the ring axis to showcase the twelve-fold symmetry. Per-chain SES surfaces reveal the active site tunnels leading to the buried catalytic centers.

name: OmpF Porin

highlight_material.residue_selection: ARG 42, ARG 82, ARG 132, LYS 16 (constriction zone L3 loop)

artistic_notes: OmpF's beta-barrel trimer is ideally viewed down the pore axis so all three channels are visible simultaneously; ss coloring makes the 16-strand antiparallel barrel staves instantly legible against coil-colored external loops. The bfactor-tinted SES overlay highlights the flexible L3 constriction loop that gates ion passage.

name: Adenylate Kinase

highlight_material.residue_selection: AP5A bisubstrate analog, GLY 10-GLY 15 P-loop, ARG 188

artistic_notes: Adenylate kinase is the textbook conformational switch enzyme; render the open and closed states side-by-side using spectrum coloring so the hinge motion from N-terminus (blue) to C-terminus (red) is immediately apparent. Highlight the P-loop (GXXXXGK motif) and the AP5A transition-state analog to anchor the catalytic mechanism visually.

name: CRISPR-Cas9

highlight_material.residue_selection: HIS 840, ASN 863, HNH domain, RuvC domain active sites, PAM duplex

artistic_notes: CRISPR-Cas9 wraps around DNA like a clam; assign the Cas9 protein a warm amber surface and render the sgRNA and target DNA in contrasting cool blues so the nucleic acid cargo is immediately distinguishable from the protein chassis. The HNH and RuvC nuclease active sites should be lit with stick-atom detail inside the semi-transparent surface to communicate the dual-scissor cleavage mechanism.

name: Ubiquitin

highlight_residues.note: K48 chains target proteins to proteasome; K63 chains signal DNA repair and NF-kB
Hydrophobic patch — canonical ubiquitin receptor binding surface

notes: Compact 76-residue beta-grasp fold. Warm amber-wheat palette evokes the ubiquitous 'molecular tag' role. K48 and K63 as contrasting spheres immediately conveys the chain-type specificity story. Electrostatic SES overlay at low opacity reveals the charged surface that discriminates UBDs.

name: Lysozyme

highlight_residues.note: Catalytic dyad: Glu35 proton donor, Asp52 stabilizes oxocarbenium transition state

highlight_residues.selection: CYS 6, CYS 127, CYS 30, CYS 115, CYS 64, CYS 80, CYS 76, CYS 94
highlight_residues.note: Four disulfide bonds that rigidify the fold and confer thermal stability

notes: Hen egg-white lysozyme — the first enzyme structure solved (1965). Parchment-ivory palette honors its historic role. Active site cleft runs between alpha and beta domains; render from the cleft side to show the catalytic residue geometry. Golden spheres on all eight disulfide cysteines emphasize the stabilization network.

name: Myoglobin

highlight_residues.note: Protoporphyrin IX heme with central iron — primary O2 binding site
Proximal His93 coordinates Fe directly; distal His64 stabilizes bound O2

notes: First protein structure ever solved (Kendrew 1958). Deep crimson palette mirrors oxymyoglobin's vivid color. High emission on heme iron captures its redox-active character. Eight alpha-helices (A-H) wrap around the heme pocket — cartoon coloring them by helix letter helps teaching the globin fold.

name: HIV-1 Protease

highlight_residues.note: Catalytic dyad from each monomer; both Asp25 residues required for acid-base catalysis

highlight_residues.selection: ILE 47, MET 46, GLY 48, ILE 50, PHE 53, ILE 54
highlight_residues.note: Flap residues 46-54 that gate substrate access; B-factor coloring reveals their high mobility

notes: Homodimeric aspartyl protease; dark navy palette communicates the pathogen context while the hot-pink flaps make resistance mutation sites immediately visible. B-factor surface overlay is critical here — the flaps are among the highest-B segments in the PDB and their motion governs drug resistance. Render from above the active site cleft to show flap symmetry.

name: EGFR Kinase

highlight_residues.note: Erlotinib occupying the ATP binding pocket — canonical EGFR inhibitor
Salt bridge Lys745-Glu762 marks active conformation; Met769 gatekeeper residue
DFG motif activation loop — DFG-in conformation shown in erlotinib-bound state

notes: Drug-target classic. Spectrum ribbon from N-lobe (blue) to C-lobe (red) makes the bilobal kinase architecture self-evident. Erlotinib rendered as prominent colored sticks in the ATP pocket anchors the therapeutic context. Activation loop DFG motif as stick highlight allows comparison to inactive DFG-out structures.

name: CYP3A4

highlight_residues.note: Iron protoporphyrin IX — the catalytic center for oxidative metabolism
Phe-cluster gateway residues that shape the promiscuous substrate cavity
Substrate cavity walls — largest P450 active site in humans

notes: Responsible for metabolizing ~50% of clinical drugs. Deep purple-maroon palette evokes the porphyrin Soret band. The cavernous active site (up to 2000 Å3) accommodates two erythromycin molecules simultaneously — a cross-section rendering showing the cavity volume is more informative than an exterior view. Heme emission highlights the iron-oxo reactive species.

name: PD-L1

highlight_residues.selection: TYR 56, GLU 58, ARG 113, MET 115, ASN 63, VAL 68
highlight_residues.note: IgV domain interface residues that contact PD-1; checkpoint blockade epitope
Atezolizumab and durvalumab contact positions — antibody drug target epitope

notes: Immune checkpoint ligand — the brake on T-cell activation. Cool teal-lavender palette conveys the immunological context. IgV beta-sandwich fold benefits from an angled view that exposes the flat face engaged by PD-1 and anti-PD-L1 antibodies. Electrostatic overlay reveals the negatively charged surface that docks against PD-1's positive patch.

name: Beta2 Adrenergic GPCR

highlight_residues.note: Carazolol occupying the orthosteric binding pocket between TM3/TM5/TM6/TM7
DRY motif at TM3/ICL2 junction — ionic lock governing receptor activation state
Ser triad in TM5 that makes hydrogen bonds to catecholamine hydroxyl groups

notes: First GPCR crystal structure with a diffusible ligand (2007, Kobilka Nobel). Dark slate palette with lipid-bilayer-evoking horizontal banding. Seven-helix bundle rendered with ss coloring so TM1-TM7 are individually legible. Cross-sectional slice view exposes the carazolol-binding cavity. DRY motif as bright spheres at cytoplasmic face marks the G-protein coupling site.

name: KcsA Potassium Channel

highlight_residues.note: TVGYG selectivity filter — backbone carbonyls mimic water hydration shell of K+

highlight_residues.selection: K+ ions S1, S2, S3, S4
highlight_residues.note: Four ion binding sites in the selectivity filter; alternating occupancy drives conduction

notes: MacKinnon Nobel (2003). Tetrameric channel viewed down the pore axis reveals 4-fold symmetry and the narrow selectivity filter. Deep blue palette mirrors the ionic/aqueous environment. K+ ions as gold metallic spheres against the blue filter create an immediate visual metaphor for selective ion conduction. Electrostatic SES shows the negative funnel that recruits cations.

name: tRNA-Phe

highlight_residues.note: Anticodon loop positions 34-36 (GAA anticodon reads Phe UUC/UUU codons)
CCA 3'-acceptor stem — site of aminoacylation by PheRS
Post-transcriptional modified bases that stabilize the L-shaped tertiary structure

notes: L-shaped cloverleaf adapter molecule, 76 nucleotides. Warm rose palette distinguishes it from DNA's canonical blue. Stick rendering with residue coloring makes the base-stacking architecture legible. Modified bases rendered as distinct spheres tell the post-transcriptional processing story. View from the side to reveal the L-shape and the spatial separation of anticodon and acceptor ends.

name: Nucleosome Core Particle

highlight_residues.note: Histone N-terminal tails — sites of acetylation, methylation, and ubiquitination marks

highlight_residues.selection: H3 LYS 4, H3 LYS 9, H3 LYS 27, H4 LYS 20
highlight_residues.note: Key lysine positions for epigenetic histone code writing/reading

notes: The fundamental unit of chromatin packaging. 146 bp DNA (shown in blue) wraps 1.65 left-handed superhelical turns around the histone octamer (warm gold). Per-chain surface coloring distinguishes H2A, H2B, H3, H4 pairs. View from above the superhelical axis to show DNA wrapping geometry. Histone tails as stick overlays communicate the epigenetic regulatory surface.

name: GroEL-GroES Chaperonin

highlight_residues.note: Apical domains form the hydrophobic substrate-binding ring and GroES contact surface
Equatorial ATP sites drive allosteric cycle between cis and trans rings

notes: The protein folding machine — 14 GroEL subunits in two stacked 7-mer rings plus 7-mer GroES cap. Graduated teal palette maps the three structural domains: dark equatorial, mid intermediate, pale apical. Cross-sectional cut view is essential to reveal the enclosed central folding cavity where substrate proteins refold in isolation from the crowded cytoplasm.

name: 26S Proteasome

highlight_residues.selection: PSMB5 THR 1, PSMB6 THR 1, PSMB7 THR 1
highlight_residues.note: Catalytic beta subunits beta1/beta2/beta5 N-terminal Thr nucleophiles; caspase/trypsin/chymotrypsin-like activities
Deubiquitylase active site in 19S lid that removes ubiquitin chains before translocation

notes: The cellular protein recycling machinery. 2.5 MDa, 33 subunits. Monochrome steel palette — the 20S barrel as dark grey cylinder, 19S cap as lighter grey — lets the molecular scale convey power without color distraction. Red accent spheres on catalytic Thr residues inside the 20S channel are visible only in cross-section, rewarding viewers who look inside. Per-chain surface coloring distinguishes alpha/beta rings.

name: RNA Polymerase II

highlight_residues.note: Active site Mg2+ coordinated by Rpb1 Asp481/Asp483 — catalytic metal for phosphodiester bond formation
Trigger loop that folds into active site upon NTP binding to promote fidelity and catalysis
Nascent RNA-template DNA hybrid in the cleft — the product of transcription

notes: 10-subunit 500 kDa transcription engine (Kornberg Nobel 2006). Navy-ocean palette suits the nucleic-acid-handling complex. Surface view from the front reveals the clamp and cleft through which DNA template threads. The Mg2+ ion as a bright metallic sphere inside the active site cleft is the visual anchor. RNA exit channel visible as a groove along the side — render in cross-section to expose the hybrid.

name: IgG1 Antibody

highlight_residues.selection: L CDR1, L CDR2, L CDR3, H CDR1, H CDR2, H CDR3
highlight_residues.note: Six CDR loops at Fab tips form the paratope — antigen binding determinant
Inter-chain disulfide bonds in the flexible hinge region connecting Fab to Fc
N-linked glycosylation site in CH2 domain — critical for Fc receptor binding and effector function

notes: The canonical Y-shaped antibody. White-steel palette with red CDR loops and blue Fc immediately communicates the functional tripartition: two Fab arms for antigen recognition, one Fc stem for effector recruitment. The flexible hinge disulfides as golden spheres mark the pivot point. Render in slight perspective tilt to reveal all four domains (VH, VL, CH1-CH3) simultaneously.

name: SARS-CoV-2 Spike Trimer

highlight_residues.note: Receptor binding domain — engages ACE2 on host cells; primary neutralizing antibody target
S1/S2 furin cleavage site and S2' site activate fusion peptide for membrane fusion
Fusion peptide that inserts into host membrane to drive membrane merger

notes: 3.5 MDa trimeric fusion machine. Three-chain prefusion trimer rendered with distinct chain colors shows the 3-fold symmetry. Red palette evokes pathogen urgency. RBDs highlighted in contrasting gold capture the most clinically relevant domains. A tilted view that shows two RBDs in 'up' and one in 'down' conformation captures the conformational heterogeneity critical for understanding immune evasion.

name: GPCR-Gs Complex

highlight_residues.note: Receptor-G protein interface: outward displacement of TM6 opens cavity for Gs alpha5 helix
Alpha5 helix insertion into receptor core — the key engagement event for receptor-G coupling
Empty nucleotide pocket in the receptor-stabilized nucleotide-free state (Gs activation intermediate)

notes: Landmark signaling complex (Kobilka second Nobel contribution, 2012). Five distinct chains (receptor, Gs-alpha, Gs-beta, Gs-gamma, nanobody) rendered in five distinct palette colors to expose every player in the ternary complex. The outward-tilted TM6 shown with cartoon inside the SES surface captures the activated receptor conformation. The empty nucleotide pocket as stick overlay communicates the transient nature of the complex.

name: Collagen Triple Helix

highlight_residues.note: Every third Gly of Gly-X-Y repeat packs into triple helix interior; Gly mutations cause osteogenesis imperfecta
Hydroxyproline (post-translational, vitamin C-dependent) stabilizes helix via water bridges

notes: The most abundant protein in the human body — an elegant supercoiled rope. Warm amber-ivory palette evokes structural connective tissue. Three chains wound in right-handed superhelix are rendered per-chain in stepped warm hues. Gly spheres as white markers on the central axis and Hyp sticks on the exterior together tell the Gly-X-Y repeat story in a single view. Elongated aspect ratio rewards a wide-format composition.

name: F-Actin Filament

highlight_residues.selection: ADP, Pi at each subunit nucleotide site
highlight_residues.note: ADP+Pi (pointed end) vs ADP (barbed end) — nucleotide state controls filament dynamics
DNase I binding loop at pointed end; mediates actin-actin longitudinal contacts in filament

notes: Cryo-EM structure of the cytoskeletal polymer. Tangerine-ember palette evokes dynamic muscular motion. The two-start helical filament viewed along its axis shows the right-handed twist. Per-subunit chain coloring in alternating shades of orange makes the helical repeat immediately visible. Nucleotide states at both ends together tell the treadmilling mechanism story in a single image.

name: Streptavidin-Biotin

highlight_residues.note: Trp cage around biotin — four tryptophans sandwich the ureido ring via van der Waals and hydrogen bonds
Hydrogen bond donors to biotin; Asn23 and Ser27 contact the ureido carbonyl oxygens
Biotin ligand — Kd ~10^-15 M, strongest known non-covalent interaction

notes: The tightest non-covalent interaction in biology. White-grey protein tetramer makes the yellow biotin ligand unmissable. The Trp cage as aromatic sticks around the biotin sphere is the key narrative element — four tryptophan residues from two subunits clamp the bicyclic ring. A monochrome grey exterior surface with a cut-away reveals the buried biotin in its aromatic embrace.

name: Cas12a (Cpf1) Endonuclease

highlight_residues.note: RuvC nuclease triad — single active site that cleaves both strands sequentially (unlike Cas9's dual nuclease)
WED and PI domains recognize the T-rich PAM on the non-template strand

notes: CRISPR-Cas12a cleaves staggered cuts and processes its own crRNA — distinct from Cas9. Deep indigo protein surface with amber crRNA distinguishes the nucleic acid from protein. The RuvC-only active site (no HNH domain) is highlighted with red spheres inside the transparent surface to emphasize the mechanistic difference from Cas9. PAM recognition domains in contrasting yellow.

name: Kinesin Motor Domain

highlight_residues.note: ATP analog AMP-PNP in the nucleotide pocket — mimics the pre-hydrolysis state
Neck linker docks onto motor domain in ATP state to generate the 8 nm power stroke
Switch I and II loops sense nucleotide state and communicate with microtubule binding surface

notes: The 8-nm molecular walker. Spectrum ribbon from N-terminus (blue) to C-terminus (red) maps the P-loop, Switch I/II, and coiled-coil stalk within a single color narrative. Orange neck linker sticks against the teal motor domain make the power-stroke element unmissable. B-factor surface overlay highlights the mobile switch loops that gate nucleotide hydrolysis and microtubule release.

name: Taq DNA Polymerase

highlight_residues.note: Catalytic Mg2+-coordinating aspartates in the palm domain — polymerase active site
Two-metal-ion catalytic mechanism — Metal A activates 3'-OH nucleophile, Metal B stabilizes triphosphate
Fingers close around incoming dNTP; thumb grips duplex DNA during synthesis

notes: The enzyme that made PCR possible (thermostable to 95°C). Right-hand metaphor: render thumb (red), palm (dark red), and fingers (pink) domains in graduated crimson tones so the molecular hand shape is immediately legible. DNA template and primer as blue sticks in the cleft create a red-on-blue composition that reads as mechanistically active. Two Mg2+ ions as metallic spheres anchor the two-metal-ion catalytic mechanism.

name: p53 DNA-Binding Domain

highlight_residues.note: Zinc coordination tetrahedral: Cys176, His179, Cys238, Cys242 — Zn2+ structural ion in L2/L3 loop region
Structural Zn2+ ion that organizes L2 and L3 loops forming the DNA-binding surface
Direct DNA base contacts; Arg248 most frequently mutated residue in human cancer

notes: Guardian of the genome. Warm spectrum ribbon from red (N-term) to blue (C-term) maps across the immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich scaffold and highlights the L2/L3 loop protrusion. Zn2+ as a bright metallic sphere at the core of the loops communicates structural dependency on zinc. Hotspot mutation residues Arg248 and Arg273 as prominent sticks tell the cancer relevance story. Electrostatic SES overlay shows the positively charged DNA-reading head.
